units.text: Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java reads and writes PDF documents, extracts text from pages, and creates or modifies form fields and annotations. It supports reading existing PDFs to extract content such as text and images, and writing new PDFs with text fragments, form fields, and widget annotations. The library operates on the pdf format and exposes the org.aspose.pdf package for Java 11 runtime.
It creates new PDF documents and edits existing ones by adding pages with Page, inserting text fragments with TextFragment, and saving the result to a file.
It extracts text from PDF pages using TextAbsorber and saves images from a specific page to PNG files using XImage.
It works with forms and annotations by creating widget annotations with customizable borders and backgrounds, adding radio button options to cells, and filling existing form fields through Form.
It renders PDF pages to raster images using device classes such as PngDevice and extracts plain text per page with TextDevice, supporting multi-page TIFF output.
It secures and optimizes documents by encrypting them with AES or RC4 using AESCipher, RC4Cipher, and StandardSecurityHandler, and reducing file size through Document.optimizeResources().
It manages document structure by reading and modifying the outline tree with OutlineCollection and OutlineItemCollection, and inspecting the logical structure tree rooted at StructTreeRoot.
This example creates a new PDF document, adds a page, and inserts a widget annotation with a red border, then prints the RGB values of the border color to the console.

The following workflows demonstrate common tasks: adding radio button options to a table cell, extracting text from a PDF, extracting images, creating a new PDF, filling form fields, preserving field insertion order, setting widget annotation background color, and configuring radio button border styles.
Add radio button options and text to a table cell.
Extract text from an existing PDF document.
Extract images from a specific page in a PDF.
Create and save a new PDF with a text fragment.
Read and update form fields in an existing AcroForm.
Insert radio button options and preserve their order.
Set and retrieve the background color of a widget annotation.
Configure and inspect the border style of a radio button option.

Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java exposes the Document class as its primary entry point for working with PDF documents, with page-level access through PageCollection and Page. Convenience operations for editing, extracting, converting, and signing PDFs are provided by dedicated facade classes such as PdfContentEditor, PdfExtractor, PdfConverter, and PdfFileSignature.
The org namespace serves as the root package for the Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java library, under which all public classes and interfaces are organized.
The org.aspose namespace contains core types and facades for PDF manipulation, including Document, PageCollection, Page, and editor classes like PdfContentEditor and PdfFileSignature.
The org.aspose.pdf namespace provides the main API surface for working with PDF content, including core classes such as Document, Page, Resources, and form-related types like Form and Field.
The getting started guide covers installation, walkthroughs, and feature guides for this library.
The how-to guides & FAQ provide task-focused answers for common PDF-processing questions.
The full API reference offers the complete, browsable reference for the public API surface.
The contributor guide provides architecture notes and conventions for contributors, including guidance for AI coding assistants.
The publishing guide describes the maintainers' release process for publishing this package to Maven Central.
The changelog documents release history and notable changes.
The in-repo getting started guide provides foundational information for beginning with the library.
The text extraction guide explains how to extract text content from PDF documents.
The annotations guide covers working with annotations in PDF documents.
The attachments guide explains how to work with file attachments in PDF documents.
The forms guide covers working with standard PDF forms.
The XFA forms guide explains how to work with XFA-based forms in PDF documents.
The metadata guide covers reading and writing document metadata in PDF files.
The PDF/A guide explains how to create and validate PDF/A compliant documents.
The document conversion guide covers converting documents between various formats and PDF.
The document generation guide explains how to create PDF documents from scratch.
The issue tracker on GitHub allows reporting bugs and requesting features.

Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java reads and writes PDF documents, converts PDF to HTML, XML, and raster images, and supports basic text extraction and form handling. It targets Java 11 and is distributed as the org.aspose:aspose-pdf-foss package at version 26.9.0.

OCR, conversion to non-PDF formats other than HTML/XML, conversion from non-PDF formats other than HTML, full XFA form rendering, and 3D annotations and PRC/U3D streams are not supported; use a dedicated OCR library instead, and rely on HTML/XML/raster output for conversions.

Text replacement with non-Latin scripts, resource optimization, and tagged PDF structure support are partially implemented: basic text replacement works but complex bidirectional reordering and shaping may differ from a reference renderer, advanced resource optimization strategies are limited, and structure tree coverage for full compliance is partial.

PDF/X validation and conversion and public-key-encrypted PDFs are supported through the same APIs used for PDF/A, but PDF/X has no dedicated test coverage and no out-of-the-box helper for public-key encryption is provided yet; additionally, PdfFileSecurity.setAllowExceptions throws UnsupportedOperationException, and a single Document instance is not thread-safe.

Aspose.PDF FOSS for Java targets Java 11 and builds with Maven 3. Tests use JUnit 5 and create PDF fixtures in-memory or via @TempDir, so the repository ships no sample PDF corpus. CI runs on every push via .github/workflows/build.yml and releases publish to Maven Central via .github/workflows/maven-central-release.yml. No required third-party package dependencies are needed.
It adds broader format conversion (including OCR and non-PDF output formats), full feature completeness, and commercial support.
LoadFormat represents the format of a PDF document being loaded.
DoWhileStmt represents a do-while statement in the JavaScript AST, containing a test condition, a body, and an optional at location.
XfaPacket represents an XFA packet with a name, document reference, dirty flag, and optional source bytes.
